title: HTTP /environments/read serves the required-vs-set table, composed into the production listener
description:
PREREQUISITE row filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-05 while planning task-ba83b202265d40d1885d3091f009b0a2 (the Environments screen), which cannot read anything without it. That row now declares dependsOn against this one.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04):
- `ls apps/daemon/src/http/ | grep -i env` returns NOTHING. No environments route exists.
- `grep -n design apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` and the equivalent for environments return nothing either.
- Child 1 task-d0c63cd8848a4da18ad3fbb8eb1d95c3 is DONE, and its own completionSummary states the scope precisely: "17 paths, all new, all under apps/daemon/src/environment/. Nothing outside that directory changed." Its "reads" are IN-PROCESS projection functions - `readEnvironmentState` (:80), `projectEnvironmentVariables` (:95), `EnvironmentReadOk` (:49), `EnvironmentReadResult` (:61) in apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts - not an HTTP surface.
So the store and the projection exist and are DONE; the operator-facing READ does not. This row closes exactly that gap, symbol by symbol, rather than letting the screen row invent a daemon route it does not own or mock one in a test.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `/environments/read` serving, per environment, the variable table as {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} and NO VALUE - plus its composition into the PRODUCTION listener, in the SAME row. Do not repeat the design-read split: task-7ca9dca3 served /design/read and task-eb2bb09d then had to exist purely to compose the port into the listener, because a served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

THE PATTERN TO FOLLOW is apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts (with its .js bridge and design-read.test.ts), composed through apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts, http-listener-guards.ts and apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts. Read all five before writing; the guard and dispatch seams are where a route silently fails to mount.

A VALUE MUST NEVER CROSS THIS BOUNDARY. The projection already returns no value; this row must not add one back in a response field, an error body, a log line or a trace. That is epic rail 3 and it is the reason this route exists as its own row rather than as a field bolted onto an existing read.
definitionOfDone: `/environments/read` serves, per environment, a variable table of {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} built from the EXISTING projection in apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts (`readEnvironmentState`, `projectEnvironmentVariables`). It reimplements no store logic - assert the reuse with a grep in the completion record.

NO VALUE CROSSES THE BOUNDARY, asserted as its own arm and not merely by inspection: seed a variable with a known distinctive value, call the route, and assert that value appears NOWHERE in the response body, in any error body, or in any log line the request emits. Repeat for the refusal paths. This is epic rail 3 and it is the whole reason the route is a separate row.

THE ROUTE IS COMPOSED INTO THE PRODUCTION LISTENER IN THIS SAME ROW - http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts / http-listener-guards.ts and daemon-entry.ts as the design-read precedent requires. Assert it is reachable from the composed production listener, not only from a hand-built test server. A served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist; that is exactly why task-eb2bb09d had to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
The response decoder contract is EXACT-KEY: an unknown key and a missing key each refuse, asserted with the specific code AND the layer that refused, never merely that it failed.

ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN is asserted with code AND layer for an unknown environment, reusing child 1's already-closed code->layer map rather than minting a second one. Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line as evidence.
taskRails: A VALUE NEVER CROSSES THIS BOUNDARY - not in a response field, not in an error body, not in a log line, not in a trace, not in a committed fixture.
SERVE AND COMPOSE IN THE SAME ROW. A route that is served but not mounted is the failure that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
REUSE the existing projection (apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts) and child 1's closed code->layer map. A second store path or a second refusal map is a rejection.
NO UI, NO PROXY PIN, NO CLIENT DECODER: the control-room half belongs to task-ba83b202265d40d1885d3091f009b0a2 and touching apps/control-room here collides in the shared worktree.
Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE THE COMPOSITION CHAIN — IT IS WIDER THAN DoD-3 NAMES. NO EDITS. This step exists because the row's most important requirement (serve AND compose in the same row) is stated against a file list that is incomplete and partly wrong, and a worker following it literally would miss the production wiring — the exact failure the row was filed to prevent. TRACE IT YOURSELF: `git grep -n 'design-read|designRead|DESIGN_READ_PATH' -- apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts`. I traced it at plan time and the SEVEN sites are: (1) `http/design-read.ts` (102 lines) + its `.js` bridge + `design-read.test.ts`; (2) `http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` (557 lines) at FIVE points — import :36, the PATH roster at :88-93, the dependency pass at :368, a method guard at :480, the dispatch branch at :554; (3) `http/http-listener.ts:158`, the optional port on the deps interface; (4) `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts` at FIVE points — import :31, the provider interface `designReads?(): DesignReadPort` :47, the resolved shape :120, a KEY ROSTER at :151, and the factory resolution :336-340; (5) `daemon-store-dependencies.ts:119`, the production provider factory; (6) `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:344` and `:504`, where the port is actually built over the store; (7) `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:183-202`, which pins the factories roster with `isDependencyProvider` and asserts `designReads: () => port` is true while `designReads: port` is FALSE — a factory, not a port. TWO CORRECTIONS TO DoD-3, and record them in the step note: it names `daemon-entry.ts`, but the file is `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts`; and it omits `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` and `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts`, which ARE the production wiring — i.e. precisely what "composed into the PRODUCTION listener, not only a hand-built test server" means. Sites (5) and (6) are the difference between this row succeeding and repeating task-eb2bb09d. (b) CONFIRM THE GAP (rail 19, both directions): `ls apps/daemon/src/http/ | grep -i env` returned NOTHING at plan time. Re-check; if a route now exists, a peer built it and re-implementing is a silent duplicate. (c) CONFIRM THE PROJECTION YOU MUST REUSE: `environment-projection.ts` — `readEnvironmentState`:80, `projectEnvironmentVariables`:95, `EnvironmentReadOk`:49, `EnvironmentReadResult`:61 — and child 1's closed code->layer map. (d) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` and note peer dirt; never revert it.

THE ROUTE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/http/environments-read.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (design-read.js sits beside design-read.ts; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Mirror `design-read.ts` (102 lines) structurally — read it first, it is the whole pattern in one file: a `*_READ_PATH` const, a `LAYER` const, a frozen codes roster, a refused() helper, an exact-key body decoder, a `*Dispatch` union with `REPLY` and `LISTENER_REFUSAL` arms, and a `handle*Request(dependencies, request)` that authenticates, checks a capability, then delegates to an injected PORT. NOTE THE SHAPE THAT KEEPS THIS TESTABLE: `DesignReadPort` is documented "Closed over a store by tests and by the composition sibling; this module does not open one." Do the same — no store handle here. THE BODY DECODER IS EXACT-KEY (DoD-4) and `designReadBodyOf` is the model, including the detail that matters: it rejects a `version` that is not a finite SAFE INTEGER so "a 1.5 cannot masquerade as ABSENT". Decide your own key set and enforce it by exact arity — an unknown key and a missing key each refuse. `projectId` comes from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL, never from the payload; design-read's header states that a payload naming it is an unknown key, and the same rule applies here. REUSE, DO NOT MINT: build the table from `readEnvironmentState` / `projectEnvironmentVariables`, and take `ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN` and its layer from child 1's closed map (DoD-5). INTRODUCE NO NEW `*_LAYER` CONSTANT — rail 5 — because a new layer literal demands a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own. The response carries {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} PER VARIABLE and NO VALUE; the projection already returns none, so the job here is not to add one back.

COMPOSE IT — ALL THE WAY TO PRODUCTION, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW. Follow the seven sites from step 1 in order; the guard and dispatch seams are where a route silently fails to mount. (1) `http-listener-read-dispatch.ts`: import the path and handler; add the path to the roster at :88-93; pass the port through at :368; add the method guard at :480 (a non-POST must refuse, not fall through); add the dispatch branch at :554. (2) `http-listener.ts:158`: add the optional port to the deps interface beside `designReads`. (3) `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts`, FIVE edits: the type import, the provider interface entry as a FACTORY (`environmentReads?(): EnvironmentReadPort` — the ops test pins that a bare port is REJECTED and only a function is accepted), the resolved shape, the KEY ROSTER at :151, and the factory resolution beside :336-340. (4) `daemon-store-dependencies.ts:119`: the production provider factory, mirroring `designReads`. (5) `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:344`/:504: build the port over the store and export it in the composition object. STEPS (4) AND (5) ARE THE ONES DoD-3 DOES NOT NAME AND THE ONES THAT DECIDE WHETHER THIS ROW SUCCEEDS — without them the route serves in a test and does not exist in the product, which is exactly why task-eb2bb09d had to exist after task-7ca9dca3. KEEP EACH EDIT MINIMAL: `http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` is 557 lines and `http-listener-guards.ts` is 411 — both already over the 400 cap at merge-base, so add the branch and nothing else, reformat nothing, and do not take the opportunity to tidy. Say in the step note whether `http-listener-guards.ts` needed an edit at all; DoD-3 names it, but the design-read trace shows no guard site there — if it does not need one, say so rather than inventing a change to match the DoD's file list.

TESTS, WITH THE NO-VALUE ARM AS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/http/environments-read.test.ts`, modelled on `design-read.test.ts`. (1) DoD-2, THE ROW'S REASON FOR EXISTING, and it must be hostile rather than confirmatory: seed a variable with a DISTINCTIVE known value, call the route, and assert that value appears NOWHERE — not in the success body, not in any refusal body, not in any log line the request emits. Serialize the whole response and grep it for the value rather than checking named fields, because a field-by-field check passes while the value rides in a field you did not think to name. REPEAT FOR THE REFUSAL PATHS: an unknown environment, a capability denial, a malformed body. The refusal paths are where a value leaks in practice, because an error message is where someone reaches for context. (2) DoD-4: exact-key decoding — an unknown key refuses, a missing key refuses, each asserted with the CODE and the LAYER, never merely that it failed. (3) DoD-5: `ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN` with code AND layer for an unknown environment, and assert the layer is one already on the roster — not a new literal. (4) DoD-1: the table is built from the existing projection — assert the served shape matches what `projectEnvironmentVariables` produces for the same seeded state, so a reimplementation would diverge and red. (5) DoD-3, THE REACHABILITY ARM: assert the route answers from the COMPOSED PRODUCTION listener, not a hand-built server. `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:139-174` is the precedent — it starts the entry with a provider and POSTs `/design/read`. Add the equivalent there, and also cover the factories-roster pin at :183-202 if the new key needs a line: that test asserts a FACTORY is accepted and a bare PORT is rejected, so a provider entry supplied as a value rather than a function fails there and nowhere else.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. MIXED: the route, its `.js` bridge and its test are NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is BLIND to them — SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id), proved in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The five composition files and `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts` are TRACKED and take an empty `git diff`. Say which proof applies to which path. THREE DRILLS: (i) THE NO-VALUE DRILL, and the row's most valuable artifact — make the route echo the plaintext value into its response (or into a refusal detail) and confirm the DoD-2 arm goes RED, with the leaked value visible in the failure output. Quote it. An arm that has never seen a leak is not evidence that it would catch one. (ii) THE COMPOSITION DRILL, which is what separates this row from task-eb2bb09d — remove ONLY the production provider entry in `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` (leaving the dispatch, the listener and the port resolution intact) and confirm the DoD-3 reachability arm reds. If it stays green, that arm is testing a hand-built server and the row has not proven the thing it was filed to prove. (iii) Remove the path from the roster at http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:88-93 and confirm a request reds — the roster and the dispatch branch are two separate edits and either alone leaves a hole. (b) GATES — standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row and DoD-6 asks you to say so rather than quote a bare count line — vitest.config.ts:32 has no `apps/**`. `wc -l` the two over-cap files before and after and confirm neither grew beyond its branch. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: a variable whose NAME is itself sensitive (the name IS published — is that intended, and does the row's contract say so); an environment with no variables (empty table, or a refusal?); a fingerprint that could be reversed for a short value (is a bare sha256 of a two-character value a disclosure — say what you concluded); the route reachable without the capability check; a value reaching a stack trace on the throwing path, not just a log line; whether `http-listener-guards.ts` genuinely needed no edit. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the SEVEN composition sites you touched, naming `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` and `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts` explicitly since DoD-3 omits them and they are the production half; the two corrections to DoD-3's file list; the grep proving the projection was reused rather than reimplemented (DoD-1); drill (i) and drill (ii) verbatim; and that no `*_LAYER` constant was introduced and no apps/control-room file was touched.

comments.content:
DoD-3's FILE LIST WOULD LEAD A WORKER STRAIGHT INTO THE FAILURE THIS ROW WAS FILED TO PREVENT. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 8 files (2 new).

The row is right that serve-and-compose must be one row. But its composition list is incomplete and partly wrong, and following it literally produces exactly the task-eb2bb09d outcome.

## The measured chain is SEVEN sites, not four

`git grep -n 'design-read|designRead|DESIGN_READ_PATH' -- apps/daemon/src`:

| site | what |
|---|---|
| `http/design-read.ts` + `.js` bridge + test | the route |
| `http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` | **five** points: import :36, PATH roster :88-93, dependency pass :368, method guard :480, dispatch branch :554 |
| `http-listener.ts:158` | optional port on the deps interface |
| `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts` | **five** points incl. a KEY ROSTER at :151 |
| **`daemon-store-dependencies.ts:119`** | **production provider factory — NOT in DoD-3** |
| **`daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:344`/:504** | **port built over the store — NOT in DoD-3** |
| `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:139-174`, `:183-202` | reachability from the real entry, plus the factories-roster pin |

**Two corrections:** DoD-3 names `daemon-entry.ts`, but the file is `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts`. And it omits the two files that *are* the production wiring — i.e. precisely what "composed into the PRODUCTION listener, not only from a hand-built test server" means.

Wire only the four named files and you get a route that answers in a test and does not exist in the product. **Drill (ii) is built to catch it:** remove only the `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` entry, leaving dispatch, listener and port resolution intact, and require the reachability arm to go red. If it stays green, that arm is testing a hand-built server and the row has not proven its own point.

**Third correction:** DoD-3 names `http-listener-guards.ts`, but the design-read trace shows **no guard site there** — the method guard lives in the dispatch file at :480. The plan tells the worker to say so rather than invent an edit to match the list.

## The provider entry must be a factory, not a port

`daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:183-202` pins `isDependencyProvider`: `designReads: () => port` passes, a bare `designReads: port` **fails**. Supplying a value reads correctly and fails only in that one test, far from the edit.

## The no-value arm has to be hostile, not confirmatory

Serialize the **whole** response and grep it for the seeded value — a field-by-field check passes while the value rides in a field nobody thought to name. And run it on the **refusal** paths too: an error message is where someone reaches for context, and it is where a value leaks in practice. Drill (i) makes the route echo the value and requires the arm to red with the leak visible.

## Smaller notes

`http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` (557) and `http-listener-guards.ts` (411) are **both already over the 400 cap at merge-base** — pre-existing, not this row's to fix, and not to be worsened. Add the branch, reformat nothing.

The PATH roster (:88-93) and the dispatch branch (:554) are two separate edits and either alone leaves a hole — drill (iii) covers the roster half.

One thing worth a conscious answer rather than silence: **the variable NAME is published even though the value is not**. That is the point of a required-vs-set table, but a name can itself be sensitive, and a sha256 fingerprint of a two-character value is closer to a disclosure than it looks. The adversarial pass asks for a stated conclusion.
